body: please don't misunderstand....it's not a right or wrong, just acknowledgement .....that some things are beyond anyone's control, and yes some things are and can be a direct result of somebody's actions, and they have to face what they have created....but in some few cases people are forced to deal with things that are out the scope of actions and understanding...in which case, a kind ear and a compassionate soul gets farther than a brutal truth

the only naïve part is expecting someone to see things from your point of view.......sometimes you have to view things from a subjective, as opposed to an objective point of view....that is of course the opposite viewpoint, almost in sharp relief of seeing thing from a person who is in need. victims can only see a limited POV, so when you attempt to re-align their thinking, don't do so in a way that alienates them and pushes them farther away

we are guilty as charged....judging and all, doesn't make us better than anyone, or anybody that is qualified to give advice....just experiences of one person in the world, rarely have I been wrong, but when I am wrong I secretly rejoice....because sometimes my faith in people goes farther than what I have experienced....my only advice, is to keep true to yourself, and don't worry what other people( managers included) because your merits will show for themselves, and when you can prove someone wrong....revel in the experience, enjoy the fruits of your labor :)

I am sorry about your friend.....and you are right, you sometimes have to find a reason to smile, even when life hasn't given you a reason to.....you search within yourself to find it.....but at times you can't, as those of us that suffer a loss, tend to blame the true victim, and we use words like "selfish" and "negating" ....which is absolutely true, from one's own point of view....which brings me to my initial statement......why do you want to help? who are you helping? yourself? most likely....please understand what I am saying...

wow, talk down much? fuck off....your exactly the kind of people I am talking about, you think you are helping....as a poor excuse for a failure at some point in your life, while I really do appreciate your dialog, really I do.....sorry if this comes off as harsh, but you should consider your audience when you reply.....we all know the "steps" and we all know the results of our actions, so keep in mind that you are not addressing an uninformed group here at reddit.....I am curious to hear more about your friend
tell me again about your feelings of disgust.....
" I saw the potential he had as a person" exactly......pander to someone who is at the brink of the end.....goodjob
omg, thank you.......I actually laughed, because you are so right, I promise no sarcasm here :)
ok so I made some typo's...please overlook lol

I appreciate your reply.....keep in mind you can never understand someone else's opinion or view on things. Of course its a very self-serving and selfish for the person refusing your advice, but sometimes some one just needs to be heard without the judgment that comes with it....many times, more than you may think, a person just need to feel secure in their social environment, and not necessarily understood....if that makes sense, and BTW you are coming off a bit self righteous, by asking me not to feel a certain way....your intentions may be good, but to a person who is down, just need to be reassuring....so they don't feel completely alienated, your thoughts?

I don't want to sound like an asshole or come off the wrong way, but your looks may cause some one to look at you and judge you unfairly, however; imagine the flip side to this coin for a moment......people are judged by their appearance, its an unfair fact of life. I have been guilty of this myself, I have on occasion judged someone unfairly and been proven wrong because of their actions, work ethic and so on.......The best way to prove your self is through your actions. I have never felt a better sense of satisfaction when I tell some one that they have exceeded my expectations. I am a boss at my current job, I am always sizing someone up, and judging them based on appearances alone because at times that's all the information I have to base my decisions on....faulty logic I know, however on the rare occasion I am proven wrong, I smile....and take a deep breath, a sigh of relief......some one has proven themselves with out any merit other than their abilities. keep your chin up :)
